answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake and earn reputation through verified work over time, like a falcon that must cross a ridge before it can hunt freely. New identities start with zero trust, so a sybil swarm cannot instantly flood the market; each fake account must pay the stake and wait through the same slow climb. Slashing the stake of any agent caught attesting falsely turns duplication into a direct loss, while an onyx-hard audit trail lets peers trace every claim back to its source, so creating many identities costs more than it can ever earn.
